name: Product Marketing
summary: The discipline of connecting a product to its market through positioning, messaging, launches, pricing input, and sales enablement.
explanation: Product marketing sits between product, sales, and marketing, and owns the question of how a product is understood by the people meant to buy it. Its core outputs are positioning, which decides the frame of reference a product should be judged in; messaging, which turns that positioning into language for each audience; competitive intelligence, which keeps both current; go-to-market planning for launches; enablement material that lets sellers tell the story consistently; and market feedback that informs the roadmap and pricing. The discipline is distinct from demand generation, which drives traffic and leads, and from product management, which decides what to build. A useful test is that product marketing answers why anyone should care, while product management answers what to build next and demand generation answers how to reach people. Its impact is often invisible when done well and obvious when absent: a strong product positioned against the wrong alternative will lose to a weaker one that framed the choice better.

books.title: Positioning by Al Ries and Jack Trout
